original_content.knowledge_point: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces
original_content.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=-x-y-z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2}-{u}^{2},\,u⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?
original_content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}-{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}-{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -2u & 1 \\ 0 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-2u & 1 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2u \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,0,\,2v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-2v,\,0,\,2v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-2v)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(2v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+4{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(-x-y-z)\,{|}_{x=u\,y={v}^{2}-{u}^{2}\,z=u} \\  & =-u-({v}^{2}-{u}^{2})-u \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}-2u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}-2u)\sqrt{8}v\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=-x-y-z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2}-{u}^{2},\,u⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ Use the scalar surface-area factor $\|r_u\times r_v\|$ with its absolute values for the stated parameter domain. What is the missing expression?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
For a scalar surface integral, the pullback integrand is $f(r(u,v))\|r_u\times r_v\|$. The derivatives and cross product are

$$r_u=(1,-2u,1),\qquad r_v=(0,2v,0),\qquad r_u\times r_v=(-2v,0,2v).$$

Thus the nonnegative area factor is

$$\|r_u\times r_v\|=\sqrt{(-2v)^2+(2v)^2}=\sqrt8\,|v|.$$

Substitution into the scalar function gives

$$f(r(u,v))=-u-(v^2-u^2)-u=u^2-v^2-2u.$$

The missing integrand for the stated general parameter domain is therefore

$$(u^2-v^2-2u)\sqrt8\,|v|.$$

The source omitted the absolute value and supplied no sign restriction on $v$. Its option $(u^2-v^2-2u)\sqrt8\,v$ is valid on a positive-$v$ patch, but fails when $v<0$: at $(u,v)=(1,-1)$ the corrected value is $-2\sqrt8$, while that source option gives $2\sqrt8$. The capture used a distinct explicit $v>0$, regular, one-to-one recovery request. This study question retains the original domain and supplies the correct absolute-value choice.

The parametrization loses rank at $v=0$. As usual, interpreting the displayed equality as an integral over the surface assumes regular patches and no multiple coverage except on negligible boundaries; the local area factor remains $\sqrt8|v|$.
